description: Thomas Grandits, Stefano Coss and Gundolf Haase publish the reference implementation of dynamic thermal-plant control for the OpenDHN heating network. The July 2025 ZIP is freely downloadable under AGPL-3.0-or-later. The describing preprint identifies Python, PyTorch automatic differentiation and L-BFGS optimisation, with 150 substations and two plants in an anonymised Verbier network. Experiments use synthetic consumer variations over 23–25 October 2021 and fifteen-minute price inputs. The code can benchmark temperature control and thermal-storage use in district-heating simulations. Limitations include fixed hydraulic flows, a modified near-stagnant substation and synthetic demand, which constrain transfer to operational control. Reported savings and runtime are author results, not independently reproduced performance. Related catalogue record data-opendhn-verbier-meshed-district-heating-benchmark covers the network inputs, not this controller. Archive contents and environment compatibility were not tested.
inputs: OpenDHN topology and steady mass flows
Synthetic consumer demand and energy prices
